key_insight: Global optimal control can reshape a globally driven superconducting processor to dramatically suppress decoherence and recover high-fidelity gates even when dissipation acts on every qubit in the device.
engineering_relevance: For superconducting quantum hardware, temporal shaping of a shared control drive offers a practical route to shorter gate sequences and better performance without isolating a protected subsystem.
method: Tensor-network simulation of a quasi-2D ladder architecture.
Modeling of amplitude-damping and dephasing noise across the full globally driven system.
Global pulse shaping to compress gate sequences and improve one- and two-qubit fidelities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified degradation of information flow and gate fidelity under noise, followed by an order-of-magnitude reduction in gate-sequence time with restored high fidelities after optimal control.
watch_item: The mitigation relies on precise global pulse design and may be sensitive to hardware constraints, since noise acts on all physical qubits including those outside the logical register.
paper_title: Mitigating quantum decoherence via global optimal control
